title: French students and unions stage nationwide economic protests

tea.why: Protesters are angered by education budget cuts, a rising cost of living, and declining public services under the government.
tea.want: Demonstrators demand more teachers, smaller classes, safer school buildings, and better economic policies.
tea.changed: Oct 18: Nationwide demonstrations escalated into widespread clashes with police, property damage, and looting.

summary: Beginning as a student movement over school conditions and teacher shortages in Créteil, demonstrations quickly expanded into a nationwide movement involving teachers, parents, university students, and trade unionists. Participants voiced strong distrust in the government, citing education cuts, increasing living costs, and declining public services. Marches across multiple cities ultimately escalated into violent clashes with police, property destruction, and widespread looting of shops and public buildings. Authorities and the CGT union reported hundreds of thousands of participants nationwide. In response, government officials condemned the severe violence, while security forces deployed tear gas and water cannons, resulting in numerous arrests and injuries among both protesters and law enforcement officers.
response: French authorities deployed police who used tear gas and water cannons against protesters. Interior Minister Laurent Nuñez reported hundreds of law enforcement injuries, while Prime Minister Sebastien Lecornu and President Emmanuel Macron condemned the extreme violence and vowed prosecution for those engaged in looting and vandalism.

arrests.text: French authorities said Sunday that nearly 1,800 people had been arrested nationwide, including 855 in the Paris region.

injuries.text: More than 500 police officers, gendarmes and firefighters were injured

deaths.text: One protester died after suffering cardiac arrest during demonstrations in Paris, authorities said.

updates.text: The movement began at a high school in Créteil with teachers and students protesting staff shortages and inadequate resources.
Nationwide demonstrations over living costs and education conditions escalated into widespread clashes, fires, and looting.
